questions.text: Over the most recent period meaningful for your business, has your commercial base — customers, users, orders, or contracted work — been growing, holding, or declining?

A.text: Declining, or no commercial base is forming

B.text: Flat, or the direction is not known because progress is not tracked

C.text: Holding steady with understood drivers, or growing but inconsistently

D.text: Growing across more than one consecutive period

E.text: Growing across more than one consecutive period, and the business can identify which specific drivers are producing it

questions.text: How does the business track its commercial progress?

A.text: No defined measures; progress is judged by impression

B.text: Some figures are looked at, but not consistently and not against any expectation

C.text: A small set of defined measures is tracked on a regular cycle

D.text: As C, and those measures are the ones that genuinely reflect this business's progress, rather than generic ones adopted because they are conventional

E.text: As D, and the measures are reviewed against expectations, with divergence investigated

questions.text: When the business wins new business, what happens to its terms and to its existing customer base?

A.text: Not known — the business does not examine what its growth costs it

B.text: New business is increasingly won on worse terms — deeper discounts, costlier acquisition, more onerous conditions — or gains are offset by losses elsewhere

C.text: Terms and the existing base are broadly holding as the business grows

D.text: The business grows while maintaining its terms and retaining its existing base, and can evidence both

E.text: As D, and growth is accompanied by improving economics or strengthening retention rather than merely stable ones

questions.text: Does the business set objectives and achieve them?

B.text: Objectives are set loosely or informally, and whether they were met is not assessed

C.text: Specific objectives are set for a defined period, and the business assesses whether they were met

D.text: As C, with a record of meeting most of them, or of understanding clearly why not

E.text: As D, and that assessment feeds into how the next period's objectives are set

questions.text: Is the business's recent progress produced by something repeatable, or by one-off events?

A.text: Progress, where it exists, has come from one-off events — a single large order, a single introduction, a favourable moment — with no repeatable mechanism

B.text: Some repeatable activity exists, but most progress still depends on one-off events

C.text: Most progress comes from activity the business can and does repeat

D.text: As C, and the business has repeated it deliberately, with comparable results more than once

E.text: As D, from more than one repeatable source, so progress does not depend on a single mechanism continuing to work
